html:
The Sora, also written Sura, were one of the Aymara-speaking lordships of the Bolivian high plateau, with their centre around Paria, near today's Oruro. Like their neighbours the Charka and Qaraqara they were part of the world of the Aymara kingdoms that rose after the fall of Tiwanaku.

In the late 1400s the Inca Empire conquered them and built an administrative centre at Paria on the royal road. Sora men served the Inca as soldiers and farmers. After the Spanish conquest they were drafted under the mita to work the silver mines of Potosí. Their descendants are among the Aymara and Quechua peoples of the region today.
